subtopics.title: Warm-Up — Concepts and the Asset Disposal

questions.question: A vehicle costing R240 000 is depreciated at 15 percent on cost and sold eight months into the year. The current-year depreciation is:
options: R24 000 — R36 000 apportioned for eight months
R36 000 — a full year regardless of the sale date

questions.question: Accumulated depreciation is R118 000 plus R24 000 for the current year. The carrying value at sale is:
options: R98 000 — cost of R240 000 minus R142 000

questions.question: The concept that forbids overstating income or assets is:
In the time-apportionment step, the mark most often lost comes from:
options: Charging a full year of depreciation instead of the months that actually ran

questions.question: Rent of R91 000 was received for fourteen months. The year's rent income and the deferral are:
options: R78 000 income; R13 000 income received in advance

questions.question: Insurance of R21 600 includes four months belonging to next year. The adjustment is:
options: Subtract R7 200 from the expense and show a prepaid expense of R7 200
Ignore it — insurance is always a full-year cost

questions.question: An R800 000 loan at 9 percent shows interest of only R66 000 recorded. The correction is:
options: Accrue a further R6 000 so the expense reaches R72 000

questions.question: Net profit before tax is R840 000. The tax line, at the company rate, is:
options: R226 800 at twenty-seven percent, leaving R613 200 after tax

subtopics.title: The Share Capital and Retained Income Notes

questions.question: After issuing 150 000 shares at R5,50 onto an opening R2 400 000 for 600 000 shares, the new average issue price is:
Sixty thousand shares are repurchased at R4,90 against a R4,30 average. The share capital note shows:
options: R258 000 out — sixty thousand at the average; the 60 cents premium goes to retained income

questions.question: The interim dividend used 750 000 shares but the final used 690 000 because:
options: The buy-back happened between the two dividends, so fewer shares remained for the final

questions.question: Opening retained income R380 000, profit after tax R613 200, buy-back premium R36 000, dividends R463 500. Closing retained income:
SARS for income tax appears in current liabilities at R16 800 because:
options: The charge of R226 800 exceeds provisional payments of R210 000 by that amount
It is the full tax charge

questions.question: The tenant's extra two months of rent land on the balance sheet as:
options: Income received in advance of R13 000 in current liabilities

questions.question: The prepaid insurance of R7 200 is shown:
options: Inside trade and other receivables in current assets

questions.question: If the balance sheet refuses to balance in the examination, the best move is:
options: Change a figure until it balances
Rule it off and move on — follow-on marks protect correct method, and the hunt costs marks elsewhere

questions.question: Tax charge R226 800, SARS owed R11 200 at the start and R16 800 at the end. Tax paid is:
options: R221 200 — charge plus opening owed minus closing owed

questions.question: Dividends paid of R417 500 consists of:
options: This year's interim plus this year's final
Last year's final of R230 000 plus this year's interim of R187 500

questions.question: Opening fixed assets R3 560 000, depreciation R130 000, disposal at carrying value R98 000, closing R3 905 000. Purchases were:
The buy-back appears in financing activities at:
options: Nothing, as buy-backs are not cash
R294 000 — the full price, because that is the cash that left

questions.question: Baobab Limited earns 16,2 percent on total capital while loans cost 12 percent. Its 0,6 to 1 gearing is:
options: Justified — each borrowed rand clears 4,2 cents, lifting return on equity above return on capital

questions.question: Karee Limited earns 10,4 percent on total capital against the same 12 percent loan rate. More borrowing would:
options: Destroy value — each borrowed rand would cost more than it earns, so the low gearing is wise

questions.question: Karee's current ratio of 4,1 to 1 is best judged as:
options: Ideal — the higher the safer, always
Lazy capital — money sleeping in stock and debtors that could fund expansion or dividends

questions.question: Karee trades at 480 cents against a net asset value of 530 cents. The discount signals:
options: A printing error in the question
That the share must be bought immediately
That net asset value is calculated wrongly
Market doubt that the assets will earn their keep — though a bidder might see a bargain

subtopics.title: The Audit Report and Governance Task

questions.question: An unqualified audit opinion states that the financial statements:
options: Fairly present the position and results, in all material respects
Are guaranteed free of any error
Show the company is well managed

questions.question: The audit report is addressed to:
options: The shareholders — the auditors work for the owners, not the managers they check

questions.question: The audit firm also runs the company's bookkeeping. The governance problem is:
options: There is no problem — it saves money
Independence is compromised — the auditors would be checking their own work
The Companies Act requires one firm for both

questions.question: A director sells shares the week before poor results are announced. This is:
options: Acceptable if the amounts are small
Insider trading — illegal use of knowledge the market lacks
